newsitem.title: UK: Brazil demand dominates sugar freight orders.
newsitem.headline: Brazil demand dominates sugar freight orders.

text.p: Demand picked up on the sugar freight market on Thursday with Brazilian ports attracting the bulk of the increased inquiry, shipbrokers said.
"It (inquiry) is quite heavy. These ships have been bumping on the bottom for some time, for those that do this kind of business," one shipbroker said.

E D & F Man quoted for 35,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Paranagua to the Black Sea for prompt dates and fixed its recent order for 18,500 tonnes in bulk from Maputo to US Gulf/Atlantic for 8/20 October.

Shipbrokers said Man also fixed 25/28,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Maceio to the Black Sea for prompt dates. Amerop was open for 16/16,500 tonnes of bulk sugar from Salaverry to US Gulf/Atlantic for 16/31 October and Czarnikow Rionda for 12/14,000 tonnes from south Brazil to east Africa with options of Red Sea and Pakistan for mid-October. Glencore and Louis Dreyfus both quoted for bagged cargoes for mid-October shipment dates.
Glencore was in the market for 13,200/13,650 tonnes from Santos to the Egyptian Mediterranean and Dreyfus for 14/15,000 tonnes from Paranagua to the Red Sea.

Tate & Lyle was open for 22,000 tonnes of bulk sugar, at five percent, from Maceio/Recife to Baltimore/New York for 20/25 October and Jean Lion for 7/12,000 tonnes from the same origins to Constanza for prompt dates.

Other fixtures included Sugar Chartering, which was said to have fixed its recent inquiry for 14,800/15,800 tonnes of bulk sugar from Maceio to US Gulf/Atlantic. Details of the rate achieved have yet to emerge.
Shipbrokers said Booker fixed 7,800 tonnes of bulk sugar on its usual Georgetown to UK/Nantes run for 14/18 October at a rate reported to be close to stg 20.
Lastly, South Africa Sugar Association (SASA) fixed 18,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Durban to the US for October dates.
